threadDescriptions.ferry-interviews: Record and transcribe former ferry workers' local-history interviews
threadDescriptions.speaker-permissions: Document what uses each ferry interview speaker permits
threadDescriptions.listening-exhibit: Build a short listening exhibit about the old ferry crossing
threadDescriptions.shed-roof: Replace a damaged panel on my garden shed roof

items.text: Ferry interview with Mr Renn: ask how the last boat was signalled in fog, then let him describe an ordinary shift. Avoid starting with the closure dispute.
items.rationale: Plans oral-history questions and interview approach.

items.text: Shed roof panel has a split around the nail by the apple tree. Measure the overlap before ordering a replacement sheet.
items.rationale: Household outbuilding repair.

items.text: Ferry voices permission sheet: distinguish archive storage, named quotation and public audio playback. Give speakers a copy with their chosen boxes marked.
items.rationale: Designs how speaker permissions are recorded.

items.text: Listening exhibit idea: visitors hear a bell, a short worker memory, then the river now. Keep the whole sequence under four minutes.
items.rationale: Defines the audio exhibit's visitor experience.

items.text: Renn recording, opening: 'You counted the bikes before the people. Once the deck got busy you couldn't see the wheels.' Note a follow-up about the ramp queue.
items.rationale: Interview content and research follow-up.

items.text: At the end of Renn's ferry interview, record his answer about the winter signal lamp, then read back the permission choices. He allows named archive access but has not agreed to public playback; put that limit on his signed sheet and the recording log.
items.rationale: Adds a concrete interview question and documents use restrictions with the speaker.

items.text: Don't use the bit about his brother yet.
items.rationale: No speaker, recording or intended use is identified.

items.text: Shed replacement sheet cut to size. The old battens are solid; replace only the two rusty fixings and add washers under the new heads.
items.rationale: Executes the roof-panel repair.

items.text: Exhibit prototype: fade the bell before the spoken voice begins. Visitors at the test table could not catch the first sentence over it.
items.rationale: Improves the audio installation mix after testing.

items.text: Permission register entry for Elsie Dane: archive access and named quotations allowed; public sound playback allowed only for the two marked excerpts. Store her marked transcript with the form.
items.rationale: Records precise scope of another speaker's authorization.

items.text: Dane transcript check: at 12:08 she says 'chain locker', not 'train locker'. Listen to the original once more before replacing the automatic transcript phrase.
items.rationale: Transcription accuracy for an oral-history recording.

items.text: Renn dates the new ferry shelter to 1964, the winter his eldest started work. Add that as his recollection, not an independently verified opening date.
items.rationale: Captures and qualifies a historical recollection.

items.text: Listening exhibit script uses Dane's marked queue excerpt and the river ambience. Total 3:42. Put a transcript at seated height beside the headphones.
items.rationale: Assembles the exhibit content and accessible companion text.

items.text: Shed roof hose test: no drip at the new panel overlap. The door still sticks, but that is an older issue; the roof patch is sound.
items.rationale: Checks the completed repair, without opening another project.

items.text: Renn returned his permission form with archive-only choices unchanged. Log the received date and keep his audio out of the public-playback approved list.
items.rationale: Confirms speaker permission limits.

items.text: The lamp was green, I think. Ask again.
items.rationale: A lamp alone lacks a named interview or purpose and the recollection is tentative.

items.text: Exhibit headphone lead snags on the table corner. Route it through a smooth guide and check a seated visitor can reach the volume control.
items.rationale: Installation usability and access improvement.

items.text: Renn phoned to correct the shelter date: it was 1962, not 1964; he had mixed it up with his son's later job. Append his correction to the interview transcript without deleting the original statement.
items.rationale: Genuine historical revision with preserved provenance.

items.text: Dane approved the exhibit's exact edited queue excerpt after hearing it. Add this approval to her permission record; it does not extend to the rest of the interview.
items.rationale: Records bounded authorization for the edited audio.

items.text: Ferry listening station final check: transcript matches the audible edit, bell is quieter, and the player restarts after the final river sound.
items.rationale: Verifies the completed exhibit's content and playback.

undo.reason: Hypothetical correction: the note records permission scope after approval; it does not edit or install the listening exhibit.
